title: Parish and Autopsy
premise: Jude Voss's photographic memory made him the town of Halloway's unofficial archive—he remembers every testimony, every alibi, every lie from the unsolved drowning of Ada Ferro seven years ago. When a corpse surfaces dressed in clothes lifted from his own closet, staged like an autopsy report come to life, Jude realizes someone is reenacting the old case with him cast as the killer. As the anniversary dinner of Ada's death approaches, Jude partners reluctantly with Ada's sister Ruth, a nurse who once loved him, to trap the true killer—Ada's grieving husband, the town's beloved doctor—who has spent seven years curating a perfect file of his own. The climax comes at the anniversary dinner, where Jude uses his memory as a weapon, reciting the doctor's own contradictions aloud before witnesses; the resolution leaves justice delivered outside a courtroom, but Jude's archive of secrets burned, and his love for Ruth finally admitted.
about_author: Mirabel Oyelaran is a former coroner's assistant who left forensic work to write mysteries about the people files forget. She lives in a coastal town much like Halloway, where she keeps meticulous notebooks she claims are entirely fictional.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Small Towns
chapters.summary: Jude Voss's POV. We meet Halloway through Jude's filing system of memories—every resident catalogued, every secret shelved. He attends a routine insurance claim and demonstrates his gift, recalling a witness statement word for word. The emotional beat is controlled loneliness: a man who remembers everything but participates in nothing, until a phone call about a body interrupts his evening.

chapters.title: Clothes from a Stranger's Closet
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. At the scene, Jude recognizes the dead man's outfit—his own missing clothes, down to a repaired cufflink. The body is posed like an autopsy diagram, a medical chart tucked in the pocket. Detective Ilsa Marsh suspects Jude himself. The beat is violation: the archive has been broken into, and the first file opened is his.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Rain
chapters.summary: Ruth Ferro's POV, first time. Ada's sister returns to Halloway for the anniversary, carrying her own incomplete memory of the drowning night. She visits the coroner's office and recognizes the staging: it mirrors her sister's autopsy report, page by page. The beat is dread—someone with access to sealed records is curating a second death.

chapters.title: The Doctor's Waiting Room
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude interviews Dr. Elias Ferro, Ada's husband, whose grief is immaculate and whose waiting room smells of the same antiseptic as the crime scene. Jude's memory flags small contradictions in the doctor's timeline. The beat is suspicion sharpening into certainty that the past was never closed—only alphabetized by the wrong person.

chapters.title: What the Witness Kept
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Ruth confronts Jude, revealing he was the last person to see Ada alive and never testified. Old love and old resentment collide. Jude confesses he stayed silent to protect someone—himself, or the town, he no longer knows. The beat is the cost of memory: he can recite that night but not explain it.

chapters.title: A Second Autopsy
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A second body appears, staged as the toxicology page of Ada's file, and this time the victim is a former juror. Marsh formally names Jude a person of interest. Ruth, torn between duty and instinct, chooses to help him off the record. The beat is alliance forged in the space where law ends.

chapters.title: The File That Fights Back
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. The pair reconstructs Ada's case from Jude's memory and Ruth's stolen coroner's copies, discovering the doctor altered the original autopsy—Ada was drugged before she drowned. But someone has been inside Ruth's room; their working copies are rearranged, annotated in a hand Jude almost recognizes. The beat is paranoia: the killer is editing them.

chapters.title: Anniversary Preparations
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The town prepares the memorial dinner; invitations arrive with Jude's name written in his own handwriting. He and Ruth lay a trap, seeding a false detail only the killer would correct. When the correction arrives by letter, Jude's memory finally matches the handwriting to the doctor's old prescription pads. The beat is the hunter becoming certain.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, climax. At the anniversary dinner, Dr. Ferro poisons the wine and plans to stage Jude's death as the file's final page. Jude stalls him by reciting the doctor's contradictions before the assembled town—every altered date, every rehearsed tear. Ferro breaks; the town, forced to witness, must choose between its beloved doctor and the truth. The beat is cathartic exposure.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV, resolution. Ferro confesses in a written statement Jude memorizes before Marsh can suppress it; justice happens in the town square, not the courthouse. Jude burns his archive of secrets, choosing presence over preservation. He and Ruth stand at the water where Ada died, finally speaking of that night aloud. The beat is release: a man who kept everything learns to keep only what matters.
